edges.description: Loss of BLM disables the BLM-TOP3A-RMI1-RMI2 dissolution complex.
Biallelic BLM loss causes the syndrome's nonmalignant manifestations, but the intervening mechanisms are not established.
Loss of anti-crossover dissolution permits excessive mitotic crossover.
Excessive interhomolog crossover increases loss of heterozygosity.
Increased LOH from mitotic recombination drives tumor susceptibility across tissues.
Genome instability produces the clinical phenotype of early and multiple malignancies.
BLM deficiency is associated with prenatal growth restriction through unknown intermediates.
Persistent postnatal growth deficiency produces short stature through unknown intermediates.
Reduced head growth is associated with BLM deficiency through unknown intermediates.
Early feeding difficulties are associated with BLM deficiency through unknown intermediates.
Gastroesophageal reflux is associated with BLM deficiency through unknown intermediates.
The recurrent long, narrow head shape is associated with BLM deficiency through unknown intermediates.
The characteristic narrow facial gestalt is associated with BLM deficiency through unknown intermediates.
Sparse subcutaneous adipose tissue is associated with BLM deficiency through unknown intermediates.
The characteristic sun-sensitive rash arises through unknown intermediates.
Telangiectasia within the characteristic rash is associated with BLM deficiency through unknown intermediates.
Reduced immunoglobulin concentrations arise through unknown intermediates.
Infection susceptibility is associated with immune abnormalities through incompletely defined intermediates.
Insulin resistance arises through unknown intermediates.
Early diabetes develops from insulin resistance through incompletely defined intermediates.
Male infertility is associated with BLM deficiency through unknown intermediates.
Premature menopause in affected women arises through unknown intermediates.
Chronic airway disease and bronchiectasis arise through unknown intermediates.
Hypothyroidism is associated with Bloom syndrome through unknown intermediates.
Elevated sister-chromatid exchange in cultured cells is a diagnostic readout of the hyper-recombination state, not a separate causal driver.

nodes.description: Subcutaneous adipose tissue is sparse through childhood and adolescence, while central adiposity can emerge in adulthood.

evidence.snippet: Subcutaneous adipose tissue is sparse throughout childhood and adolescence, but adults may develop central obesity.

nodes.description: Recurrent or chronic pulmonary disease is assessed at each visit. Bronchiectasis care can include cough-assist devices, vibration vests, and daily nasal lavage for mucociliary clearance.

evidence.snippet: Cough assist devices, vibration vests, and daily nasal lavage for mucociliary clearance for bronchiectasis.

evidence.reference_title: The Bloom's syndrome gene product is homologous to RecQ helicases.
evidence.snippet: The presence of chain-terminating mutations in the candidate gene in persons with BS proved that it was BLM.

evidence.reference_title: Bloom's Syndrome: Clinical Spectrum, Molecular Pathogenesis, and Cancer Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: A common founder mutation designated blmAsh is present in about 1 in 100 persons of Eastern European Jewish ancestry, and there are additional recurrent founder mutations among other populations.

nodes.description: Biallelic pathogenic variants abolish or severely impair the BLM RecQ helicase. This is the initiating lesion for the chromosome-instability phenotype, while the routes to most nonmalignant manifestations remain unresolved.

evidence.reference_title: The Bloom's syndrome gene product is homologous to RecQ helicases.
evidence.snippet: The presence of chain-terminating mutations in the candidate gene in persons with BS proved that it was BLM.

nodes.description: Chronic bronchitis and bronchiectasis are common; progressive pulmonary failure can be fatal.

evidence.snippet: Chronic bronchitis and bronchiectasis are common, and pulmonary failure has been the cause of death in six persons.

nodes.description: Cultured cells show strikingly elevated sister-chromatid exchanges and a broader chromosome-instability phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Bloom's Syndrome: Clinical Spectrum, Molecular Pathogenesis, and Cancer Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: The absence of a functional BLM protein causes chromosome instability, excessive homologous recombination, and a greatly increased number of sister chromatid exchanges that are pathognomonic of the syndrome.

reports_on.interpretation: Elevated sister-chromatid exchange in cultured cells is a diagnostic readout of the hyper-recombination state, not a separate causal driver.

nodes.description: A sun-sensitive, usually telangiectatic facial rash commonly emerges after sun exposure in the first or second year of life, with variable severity.

evidence.snippet: typically following sun exposure during the first or second year of life, a red, sun-sensitive rash appears on the nose and cheeks

nodes.description: Diabetes resembles type 2 diabetes mechanistically but occurs much earlier and often despite low body mass index.

evidence.snippet: Diabetes has been diagnosed in 51 of 294 persons in the Bloom Syndrome Registry (17.3%) at a mean age of 26.2 years (range: 4-48 years).

nodes.description: The head shape is often long and narrow.

evidence.snippet: The head shape is often described as long and narrow

nodes.description: Accumulating somatic genome alterations produce a broad, early-onset cancer predisposition affecting hematologic and solid-tumor lineages, often with multiple primary cancers in one person.

evidence.reference_title: Age of first cancer diagnosis and survival in Bloom syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Among the 290 individuals in the BSR, 155 (53%) participants developed 251 malignant neoplasms; 100 (65%) were diagnosed with 1 malignancy, whereas the remaining 55 (35%) developed multiple malignancies.

nodes.description: BLM normally cooperates with TOP3A, RMI1, and RMI2 in the BTRR complex to dissolve double Holliday junctions without crossover. Loss of BLM removes this anti-crossover genome-maintenance activity.

biological_processes: double-strand break repair via homologous recombination

evidence.reference_title: The Bloom's syndrome helicase suppresses crossing over during homologous recombination.
evidence.snippet: The mechanism, which we term double-junction dissolution, is distinct from classical Holliday junction resolution and prevents exchange of flanking sequences.

evidence.reference_title: TopBP1 interacts with BLM to maintain genome stability but is dispensable for preventing BLM degradation.
evidence.snippet: Finally, we identify critical residues that mediate interactions between TopBP1 and MDC1, and between BLM and TOP3A/RMI1/RMI2.

nodes.description: Feeding problems commonly begin in infancy or early childhood and can include slow eating, reduced appetite, restricted food variety, and need for enteral support in some affected children.

evidence.snippet: Most parents report that feeding is an issue for their newborns, infants, and young children.
Many infants have had gastrostomy tubes placed.
The child with BSyn characteristically eats slowly, has a decreased appetite, and eats a limited variety of foods.

nodes.description: Gastroesophageal reflux is a common contributor to early feeding problems.

evidence.snippet: Gastroesophageal reflux is common and may contribute to the feeding issues.

nodes.description: One or more plasma immunoglobulin concentrations are usually low, most often IgM and IgA, within a broader variable adaptive immune phenotype.

evidence.snippet: the concentration of one or more of the plasma immunoglobulins is usually abnormally low. IgM and IgA levels are most commonly affected.

nodes.description: Hypothyroidism can occur at an unusually early age and is monitored from childhood.

evidence.snippet: Serious medical complications that are more common than in the general population and that also appear at unusually early ages include cancer of a wide variety of types and anatomic sites, diabetes mellitus as a result of insulin resistance, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and hypothyroidism.

nodes.description: Individuals with recurrent infections and documented humoral immune defects may receive immunoglobulin replacement to reduce infection frequency and severity; this is not a universal treatment for every affected person.

evidence.snippet: Individuals with recurrent infections and defects in humoral immunity may be treated with immunoglobulins to decrease frequency and severity of infections.

nodes.description: Excessive interhomolog crossover recurrently removes heterozygosity across the genome, increasing the probability that cancer-relevant somatic variants become homozygous.

evidence.reference_title: Interhomolog recombination and loss of heterozygosity in wild-type and Bloom syndrome helicase (BLM)-deficient mammalian cells.
evidence.snippet: LOH is increased by fivefold or more, implying significantly increased interhomolog crossing over.

nodes.description: Cancer treatment is individualized by oncology specialists, commonly with reduced dosage or duration because standard regimens can cause excessive toxicity. Ionizing radiation and alkylating agents are minimized or avoided when clinically feasible; undertreatment is also a risk, so no universal dose reduction is asserted.

evidence.snippet: In persons with cancer, modification of chemotherapy dosage and duration per oncologist.
Alkylating agents and radiation therapy are considered high risk and are avoided when possible in those with BSyn.

nodes.description: Insulin resistance can begin in childhood and precedes the early-onset diabetes phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Bloom syndrome (BSyn) is characterized by severe pre- and postnatal growth deficiency, immune abnormalities, sensitivity to sunlight, insulin resistance, and a high risk for many cancers that occur at an early age.

nodes.description: Most evaluated males have azoospermia or severe oligospermia; confirmed paternity is exceptional.

evidence.snippet: men tend to be infertile, with only one confirmed case of paternity.

nodes.description: Head circumference is persistently below normal, although intellectual ability is usually preserved.

evidence.snippet: Despite their very small head circumference, most affected individuals have normal intellectual ability.

nodes.description: BLM-deficient cells undergo excessive homologous recombination and mitotic crossover. Elevated sister-chromatid exchange is modeled as a cellular readout of this state rather than as a separate causal driver.

evidence.reference_title: Bloom's Syndrome: Clinical Spectrum, Molecular Pathogenesis, and Cancer Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: The absence of a functional BLM protein causes chromosome instability, excessive homologous recombination, and a greatly increased number of sister chromatid exchanges that are pathognomonic of the syndrome.

nodes.description: A narrow face with underdeveloped malar and mandibular prominences is a recurrent facial gestalt, often with retrognathia or micrognathia.

evidence.snippet: More commonly, the face appears narrow, with underdeveloped malar and mandibular prominences and retrognathia or micrognathia

nodes.description: Hematologic and solid malignancies arise early, and multiple primary cancers are common among affected people.

evidence.reference_title: Age of first cancer diagnosis and survival in Bloom syndrome.
evidence.snippet: The cumulative incidence of any malignancy by age 40 was 83%.

nodes.description: Use calorie-dense formulas or foods when appropriate, involve gastroenterology or feeding specialists, and treat gastroesophageal reflux as needed.

evidence.snippet: Increased-calorie-density formulas and foods may promote weight gain; consultation with gastroenterologist or feeding specialist and treatment for gastroesophageal reflux disease as needed; standard dietary treatment for dyslipidemia.

nodes.description: Affected women can be fertile but commonly experience premature menopause.

evidence.snippet: Women may be fertile but often have early menopause

nodes.description: Growth deficiency begins prenatally, with affected fetuses typically small for gestational age.

evidence.snippet: Bloom syndrome (BSyn) is characterized by severe pre- and postnatal growth deficiency
The most consistent clinical feature of BSyn seen throughout all stages of life is growth deficiency affecting height, weight, and head circumference.

nodes.description: Children experience more infections than unaffected peers, although opportunistic infection is not characteristic and severe invasive infection is uncommon.

evidence.snippet: Parents of children with BSyn report that their affected children have more childhood infections than their sibs and peers

nodes.description: Avoid excessive ultraviolet exposure, use sun-protective clothing and a broad-brimmed hat, wear UV-blocking sunglasses, and apply broad-spectrum sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher.

evidence.snippet: Skin protection, including avoiding excessive sun exposure, sun-protective clothing and broad-brimmed hat, UV-blocking sunglasses, and use of broad-spectrum sunscreen with SPF of at least 30

nodes.description: Persistent postnatal growth deficiency affects linear growth throughout childhood and adulthood.

evidence.snippet: The most consistent clinical feature of BSyn seen throughout all stages of life is growth deficiency affecting height, weight, and head circumference.

nodes.description: The characteristic sun-sensitive rash is usually telangiectatic, although poikilodermatous morphology can occur.

evidence.snippet: It is usually characterized by telangiectasia but in others is described as poikiloderma.

nodes.description: Bloom syndrome has characteristic growth, craniofacial, gastrointestinal, dermatologic, immune, metabolic, reproductive, pulmonary, and thyroid manifestations, but current evidence does not establish a single downstream molecular route from BLM loss to these findings.

evidence.snippet: remains unexplained, as do the medical complications of BSyn other than cancer.
